name: Body contouring wood therapy

lead: Wood therapy, or maderotherapy, is a body-contouring massage in which a therapist presses and rolls shaped wooden tools over the thighs, hips, stomach and buttocks. Clinics offer it to improve the look of cellulite, firm the skin and support circulation and lymph drainage.

Providers describe results as visible smoothing and a toned contour. A board-certified plastic surgeon quoted by Blavity says there is not strong scientific evidence that it permanently reduces cellulite or fat, and that visible effects are likely temporary.

paras: Sessions run about 45 to 60 minutes. Therapists apply rhythmic pressure with rollers, cups and sculpted tools. Clinics suggest repeat sessions and pairing them with diet and exercise.

Bruising and irritation from firm pressure are the main reported effects. Dr. Meegan Gruber notes darker skin may be prone to hyperpigmentation, and people with keloids, varicose veins, clotting disorders, eczema or psoriasis are advised to consult a professional first.

angle.text: Clients use it to temporarily smooth cellulite and sharpen contour before events. Any visible change is described by clinicians as short-lived.

lead: Wood therapy, also called maderotherapy or maderoterapia, is a massage technique using specially shaped wooden tools pressed into the skin and underlying tissue to contour the body [1][2].

Clinics claim it stimulates lymphatic drainage and circulation, helps break down localised fat and reduces the look of cellulite [1][2]. People book it for smoother-looking thighs and a more defined waist.

Clinics describe results as temporary and recommend maintenance sessions [1]. A plastic surgeon quoted by Blavity said there is not strong scientific evidence that it permanently reduces cellulite or fat deposits [2].

paras: Therapists use ergonomically shaped wooden utensils to apply rhythmic, targeted pressure on specific body areas [1]. Aftercare advice from one clinic includes drinking water, balanced diet and exercise, and avoiding harsh products on treated areas for 24 hours [1].

Providers claim fat breakdown, cellulite reduction, toning and lymphatic drainage [1][2]. Dr. Meegan Gruber told Blavity wood therapy "doesn't precisely melt fat away" and that any change is likely temporary; she said liposuction and surgery give the most predictable long-term results and that it can be a relaxing self-care addition [2].

Firm pressure can cause bruising or irritation, especially on sensitive skin. Darker skin tones may be more prone to hyperpigmentation after skin trauma. People with keloids, varicose veins, clotting disorders, eczema or psoriasis are advised to be cautious [2].
